newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Bank Negara urges mergers among Malaysian banks.
newsitem.headline: Bank Negara urges mergers among Malaysian banks.

text.p: Bank Negara Malaysia's Governor Ahmad Mohd Don on Monday urged local banks to consider mergers among themselves in order to gain in size and compete in the international markets.

"For those who do not have the size but aspire to play a bigger role, the Governor urged these financial institutions to seriously consider the option of merger," a statement from the central bank said.
The Governor was speaking at the opening of the central bank's eleventh annual conference with the chief executives of all the country's financial institutions.

The Governor told bankers that size was becoming increasingly important to compete in the financial markets and even large banks in more developed economies were recognising the need to merge, the statement said.
It said mergers would allow companies to retain their market dominance and enjoy the benefits of synergy and economies of scale.
"An institution with a larger capital base will be able to assume greater risk and be more willing to expand its operations and venture into new business," the statement quoted him as saying.

The chief executives were also told that the central bank's policy was towards greater self-regulation in the banking industry and making financial institutions more market driven organisations, the statement said.
It said the central bank would set up benchmarks to measure profitability, growth potential, liquidity and asset quality among banks.
